headline: Iran nuclear talks collapse; Gulf posturing begins
description: Breakdown of nuclear negotiations leads to increased military posturing in the Persian Gulf. Oil markets begin pricing supply risk - though WTI is still near a 12-month low of $57 and had fallen roughly 20% over 2025.

headline: Supreme Court strikes down the IEEPA tariffs, 6-3
description: Learning Resources v. Trump holds that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not authorize tariffs. Collection ends February 24. Average import tariffs fall roughly 4.8 percentage points - eight days before the Iran strikes.

headline: Section 122 blanket 10% surcharge replaces the struck-down tariffs
description: Proclamation 11012 imposes a 10 percent ad valorem surcharge on roughly $1.0 trillion of imports. Energy and energy products are exempted verbatim. The surcharge expires by statute on July 24, 2026.

headline: US and Israel strike Iran; Strait of Hormuz closes
description: Coordinated strikes begin. The IRGC declares the Strait of Hormuz closed within days, removing roughly 13.8 million barrels per day of gross transit - about 20 percent of world oil trade. WTI begins a five-week climb from $67 to $114.

headline: Platts suspends all Hormuz-transiting grades from the Dubai benchmark
description: The price reporting agency cuts deliverable grades from five to two, leaving only Murban (loading ex-Fujairah) and Oman. The Dubai benchmark after this date measures a structurally different basket than before it.

headline: IEA members agree to release 400 million barrels
description: The largest coordinated release in the agency's 52-year history - roughly one third of government stockpiles across 32 nations. The US share is 172 million barrels over about 120 days. Expert estimates put the short-term price effect near $2 per barrel.

headline: Two-week ceasefire agreed; Hormuz reopens partially
description: The US and Iran agree to a two-week ceasefire including reopening of the Strait. Oil plunges below $100 from its $114 peak.

headline: Physical crude trades $35 above paper - a record
description: North Sea Dated commands a record $35 per barrel premium over ICE Brent futures. April's Dated range spans roughly $50 intramonth, the widest ever recorded. The premium collapses to $3 by early May.

headline: 60-day ceasefire and US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding
description: Vessels transiting the Strait must coordinate with Iran's newly established Persian Gulf Strait Authority. Transits triple within days; Hormuz oil flow recovers to about 4.8 million barrels per day. WTI falls all the way back to $69.74 - below its pre-war level.

headline: US strikes Iran again; the ceasefire is declared over
description: Retaliation for attacks on three commercial ships in the Strait. WTI rises 4.4 percent to $73.52 and Brent 5.2 percent to $78.02 on the day.

headline: Three tankers attacked in a single day; a seafarer killed
description: Stolt Magnesium, Mombasa B and Al Bahyah are struck in and around the strait. One crew member is killed on Mombasa B and eight injured. The IRGC says it targeted vessels using mined routes.

headline: Attacks on Saudi tankers; war risk premiums hit 7.5-10% of hull value
description: Marsh reports war risk insurance at 7.5 to 10 percent of hull value for a single transit, up from 1 to 3 percent weeks earlier and 0.25 percent before the war. On a $100 million tanker that is $7.5-10 million per voyage.

headline: Section 122 surcharge expires; Section 301 becomes the baseline
description: The 10 percent blanket surcharge lapses by statute after 150 days. Section 301 forced-labor tariffs at 10 and 12.5 percent across roughly 99 percent of imports become the operative regime.

headline: Escalation threats push Brent back above $90
description: Renewed threats against Iran drive Brent above $90 as tanker attacks in the Strait continue and fighting spreads toward the Red Sea.

headline: A month-long lull in US-Iran strikes begins; attacks on merchant ships continue
description: No large US or Iranian military exchanges for the month. Thirteen commercial vessels are nonetheless struck in August. The strait stays effectively closed: IMF PortWatch counts single-digit daily transits against a pre-war average of about 83.

headline: July CPI: 3.4% headline, 2.5% core, energy +14.7%
description: Headline and core both ease a tenth from June. Energy falls 1.5% on the month but remains 14.7% above a year earlier. The breadth test still reads as a tail shock: median CPI 2.7%.

headline: IEA: Gulf exports down 2.1 mb/d; world supply to fall 4.3 mb/d in 2026
description: The August Oil Market Report says the strait was 'effectively closed again in early July'. Observed stocks have drawn 410 million barrels since February. World demand is now forecast to fall 1.6 mb/d this year.

headline: MV Minoan Dignity struck, one crew killed, on the day the President says the strait is 'open and operating'
description: The bulk carrier is abandoned after an Iranian strike. Lloyd's List Intelligence counts about 14 non-Iranian transits a day that week against roughly 100 before the war.

headline: US Navy says it has cleared mines from the strait
description: Officials confirm underwater drones identified more than 100 suspected mines. Transits do not recover: PortWatch counts four vessels that day.

headline: Saudi tanker Sidr struck; two crew killed. Thirteen merchant ships hit in August
description: The deadliest attack of the month closes it. WTI ends August at $87.03, up from $69.74 at the July ceasefire low.

headline: US and Iran trade strikes in the strait; the August lull ends
description: Renewed exchanges after a month of quiet. WTI spot closes $91.48, up 5.1% on the day; Brent $96.02. Event added on 5 September 2026 with the price path already visible -- the sign is theory-driven (escalation raises prices) but this event is not pre-registered in the way the first six were.

headline: Dutch central bank confirms it moved 86 tonnes of gold out of New York and Ottawa
description: De Nederlandsche Bank cites 'increasing geopolitical unrest'. New York's share of Dutch reserves falls from 31% to 18.5%. The Fed's own custody table shows foreign gold under earmark down about 160 tonnes since August 2025.

headline: August payrolls +162,000, the best month in five; long-term unemployed 27%
description: Well above the 53,000 consensus. Unemployment 4.1%. One strong month lifts the term average to about 42,000 a month against 321,000 in the previous term. Hires rate 3.2%, quits 1.9%: still low-fire, low-hire.
